title.value: MFMCNS: a multi-feature and multi-classifier network-based system for ransomworm detection
HFL-RD: Heterogeneous Federated Learning-Empowered Ransomware Detection via APIs and Traffic Features

authors.value: Almashhadani, A.O.; Carlin, D.; Kaiiali, M.; Sezer, S.
Lan, K.; Li, G.; Huang, W.; Li, J.

journal.value: Computers & Security (Elsevier), Article 102860, published online 28 July 2022
IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management, published online 29 May 2025

quartile_sjr.value: Q1 (Scimago SJR 2022: SJR 1.605; Q1 in Computer Science (miscellaneous) and Law)
Q1 (Scimago SJR 2025: SJR 1.389; Q1 in Computer Networks and Communications and Electrical and Electronic Engineering)

source_database.value: ScienceDirect (Elsevier); DOI 10.1016/j.cose.2022.102860; cross-verified via Scopus-indexed citation records

study_type.value: Empirical experiment / system design: network traffic behavioural analysis and multi-classifier fusion system, evaluated on WannaCry and NotPetya campaign traffic
Empirical experiment / system design: heterogeneous federated learning detection scheme combining network (C&C) and endpoint (API) features, evaluated on public ransomware/benign sample collections

methodology.value: Comprehensive behavioural analysis of ransomworm (self-propagating ransomware) network traffic using WannaCry and NotPetya as case studies. Two independent feature sets are extracted at two flow levels: session-based and time-based; an independent classifier is built on each set; MFMCNS runs the classifiers in parallel and combines their decisions with a fusion rule to improve reliability, enabling detection while the worm spreads across the network before payload execution.

Heterogeneous federated learning scheme (HFL-RD) integrating (a) Command-and-Control (C&C) traffic behaviour analysis and (b) local API call operation analysis to capture concealed ransomware characteristics; one-dimensional convolution pre-processing of raw traffic preserves structural network features; dynamic regularisation methods and penalty terms resolve the non-IID problem when aggregating ransomware features across federated clients. Experimental dataset: 300 runnable ransomware samples from 30 families plus 200 benign software samples from 7 categories gathered from three public websites.

key_findings.value: MFMCNS proved reliable with high detection accuracy against ransomworm propagation traffic (WannaCry, NotPetya); combining session-based and time-based flow classifiers through a fusion rule improves reliability over single-view network detection; network-based detection can catch ransomworm activity before the payload executes on new hosts.

HFL-RD obtained accuracy over 95% and outperformed existing methods; for unknown ransomware variants it demonstrated superior detection capability in terms of detection time and number of file corruptions; the combination of C&C traffic analysis with API call analysis captures covert evolution characteristics of advanced ransomware that single-view methods miss.

limitations.value: Acknowledged/observed: evaluation limited to two worm-propagating campaigns (WannaCry, NotPetya); method targets propagation-phase traffic, so ransomware without self-spreading behaviour (classic crypto-lockers) is not the detection target; specific accuracy figures vary by flow level and are reported per classifier rather than as a single unified benchmark.

Acknowledged/observed: federated architecture introduces communication/training overhead and assumes multiple participating clients; requires joint deployment of endpoint API telemetry and network monitoring; evaluation uses publicly downloadable samples rather than live enterprise campaigns; exact false-positive rate under production traffic load is not characterised in the abstract-level results.

research_gaps.value: Gap addressed: host-based methods only detect after infection and payload execution, whereas network-based analysis of ransomworm propagation enables pre-execution early warning. Remaining gaps: generalisation beyond WannaCry/NotPetya-style worms, robustness to encryption of propagation traffic, and larger multi-family campaign evaluation.

Gap addressed: traditional methods treat external (network) and internal (endpoint) ransomware behaviours separately, missing covert evolution of advanced ransomware; federated learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative detection across clients with non-IID ransomware data. Remaining gaps: scaling to more heterogeneous clients, adversarial robustness of the federated model, and real-world deployment validation.

inclusion_rationale.value: Passes: published 2022, Computers & Security is SJR Q1 (1.605, 2022), sourced from ScienceDirect (allowed database); anchors the network IDS pillar for ransomware campaign (ransomworm propagation) detection.

Passes: published 2025, IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management is SJR Q1 (1.389, 2025), sourced from IEEE Xplore (allowed database); provides the most recent network+endpoint hybrid detection record, extending the cluster's temporal coverage to 2025.

platform_environment.value: Network-level (enterprise/campus networks); campaign targets are Windows systems (WannaCry, NotPetya)
Network + endpoint hybrid: C&C traffic monitoring at network level plus local API call analysis on endpoints (Windows-oriented ransomware samples)

kill_chain_stage.value: Pre-encryption / pre-execution: detects ransomworm propagation traffic as it spreads to infect other hosts, before payload (encryption) runs on new victims
Pre-encryption (C&C communication stage, T1486-adjacent command channel) combined with during-encryption detection via local API call sequences (T1485)

dataset_benchmark.value: Own PCAP-based traffic captures of WannaCry and NotPetya propagation plus benign background traffic; not stated to be publicly open-sourced

Dataset assembled from three public websites: 300 runnable ransomware samples from 30 families and 200 benign samples from 7 categories; constituent sources are public but the assembled corpus is not stated to be released as a unified open dataset

evaluation_metrics.value: Detection accuracy per flow-level classifier (session-based and time-based) and for the fused MFMCNS system; reliability of the fusion rule; specific unified accuracy figure is reported inside the paper's evaluation section rather than the abstract
Detection accuracy (>95%); detection time for unknown variants; number of file corruptions before detection; comparative performance against existing methods

reproducibility.value: Moderate risk: methodology (feature sets, classifier fusion) is described in reproducible detail, but the WannaCry/NotPetya capture corpus is not clearly published; comparison baselines are the component classifiers rather than external state-of-the-art systems

Moderate risk: sample counts (300 ransomware / 30 families / 200 benign) and federated design are documented and constituent sources are public, but the assembled dataset, federated client configuration and code are not stated to be released; comparisons against existing methods are reported without shared benchmarks

threat_actor_fields.value: Partially applicable: analyses WannaCry and NotPetya campaign traffic as case studies (well-known campaign malware), but performs no actor attribution, leak-site analysis or wallet tracing
Not applicable: no RaaS group naming, leak-site evidence or payment-wallet tracing; 30 ransomware families used as detection targets without actor attribution

excluded_records.actual_record: Three papers retained: Berrueta et al. (ESWA 2022), Almashhadani et al. (C&S 2022), Lan et al. (IEEE TNSM 2025)
excluded_records.reason: All three are SJR Q1 journal papers from allowed databases (ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore), within 2022-2026, and squarely on encrypted-traffic analysis / network IDS for ransomware. No candidate in this cluster required exclusion; conference papers encountered during search (e.g., IEEE CNS 2024 context-aware detection, IEEE CSR 2023 GMM-HMM, C4D 2025 deep-learning encrypted traffic) were not retained because they are non-SJR-indexed conference proceedings.
